How to Buy Tax Sale Properties in Robertson County, Tennessee

Looking to invest in property through tax sales? Robertson County, Tennessee might be a smart place to start. The county runs yearly tax deed auctions for properties with unpaid taxes. These auctions give buyers a chance to purchase real estate at a discount—sometimes well below market value.

How to Participate in Robertson County’s Tax Sale

1. Register Ahead of Time

Visit GovEase and set up an account. You’ll need to upload a government-issued ID, a signed W-9, and proof of funds. If you’re bidding as a business, include your business documents.

2. Do Your Homework

Use the Robertson County Property Assessor’s site to check property records, lot size, ownership status, and possible liens.

3. Bid Online

Log in early on auction day. Bidding starts at 10:01 AM CT. Bids begin at the total amount due in back taxes and court fees. Highest bid wins, pending court approval.

4. Pay by 5:00 PM CT

If you win, your full payment is due the same day through ACH or wire transfer. No extensions or exceptions.

5. Wait Out the Redemption Period

Tennessee law gives the original owner up to one year to redeem the property. If that happens, you get your payment refunded, but not the property. If they don’t redeem, you can begin the process of securing a tax deed.

Quick Overview: Robertson County Tax Deed Sales

Why Investors Like Robertson County

  • Online access makes the process convenient
  • Low competition due to only one auction per year
  • Close to Nashville, making it attractive for commuters
  • Flexible land use for rural, residential, or commercial development
  • Growing demand for farmland and larger parcels

Important Notes Before You Bid

  • Properties sell as-is, with no warranties
  • The county does not guarantee a clean title
  • You may need a quiet title suit to resell or insure the property
  • Some properties may carry other liens
  • Do a full title search or consult an attorney beforehand

Local Real Estate Facts

  • Commuter-Friendly: Robertson is just north of Nashville and popular with people working in the city
  • Farm-Friendly: Many buyers are looking for agricultural land
  • Affordable: Home prices remain more reasonable compared to urban areas
  • Charming Towns: Areas like Springfield feature historic homes and walkable downtowns
  • Zoning Flexibility: Allows mixed uses, good for investors with varied goals

Where It All Happens

Pro Tips for First-Time Bidders

  • Sign up early and complete all registration steps
  • Review every property before bidding
  • Set auction reminders and keep an eye on the calendar
  • Track your investments and court updates after the sale
  • Talk to a local attorney for legal help with titles or evictions

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I attend the auction in person?
No, the sale is fully online through GovEase.

Do I have to live in Tennessee?
No. Anyone can register and bid—including out-of-state and international buyers.

Can I finance my purchase?
No. You must pay in full on auction day via ACH or wire.

When do I take ownership?
After the 1-year redemption period ends and any legal title issues are resolved.

Can I get title insurance right away?
Usually not. Most properties will require a quiet title action first.

How will I know if the property is redeemed?
The county will notify you. If the owner redeems, you get a refund of your payment.

With its once-a-year online sale, low entry point, and strong real estate market, it’s worth keeping your eye on. Just remember to register early, research well, and stay organized throughout the process.
